edges: Input IDs, positions and state handles

traces.title: One request
traces.intro: Follow a prompt through its first token and the next decode step.
steps: Render the declared template and encode text to token IDs.
Admit the request and assemble positions, sequence IDs and state handles.
Prefill the prompt and advance the committed position.
Project the final hidden state into vocabulary logits.
Apply the sampling contract and commit a token. Feed that token and its position to the next decode iteration.
Decode the committed token, buffer incomplete text and stream the response.
On stop or cancellation, retire the sequence and release its claims after outstanding work completes.

traces.title: One MoE token
traces.intro: Follow authoritative routing through weight readiness and the inverse token permutation.
steps: Rank routed experts with the checkpoint rule. Record selected IDs and aligned mixture weights.
Pack rows by expert and preserve the inverse mapping.
Force an incorrect prefetch. Join or fetch the actual selected weights and wait for readiness.
Evaluate each selected expert’s gate, up and down projections.
Execute the shared branch if the checkpoint declares it. Its width and gate are independent of routed k.
Restore token order, weight each routed contribution and add the declared shared contribution. Compare against an unfused reference.

traces.title: Slow decode
traces.intro: Use a matched workload. Start with the symptom and distinguish queue delay, weight waits and device execution.
steps: Separate time to first token from steady inter-token gaps. Record client and engine clock boundaries.
Inspect ready-to-run delay, active sequences and token budget. Long queue wait with idle GPU time suggests admission or host scheduling.
Correlate demand timestamps with weight-ready events. Count missed bytes, wait time and overlap at the actual tier boundary.
Compare CPU submission, device start and completion. Inspect occupancy and measured bandwidth at the observed shape.
Repeat with fixed input lengths, concurrency and cache state. Attribute nested or overlapping intervals on a timeline before ranking causes.
